title: Heat exchanger duty
promptExcerpt: [redacted private prompt] Heat exchanger duty — see private gauntlet pack.
modelOutput:
duty
Q = m_hot × cp_hot × (T_in − T_out)
  = (12,000 kg/h) × (2.1 kJ/kg·K) × (95 − 45 K)
  = 1,260,000 kJ/h ÷ 3,600 s/h
  = 350 kW.

cw_flow
Minimum flow uses the maximum permitted CW outlet temperature, 40°C.
m_CW = Q / (cp_water × ΔT_water)
     = 1,260,000 kJ/h / (4.18 kJ/kg·K × 15 K)
     ≈ 20,100 kg/h.

area_ballpark
Using the supplied ΔT_lm ≈ 20 K as the effective driving force:
A = Q / (U × ΔT_lm)
  = 350,000 W / (400 W/m²·K × 20 K)
  ≈ 44 m².
Yes—a 1-shell-pass/2-tube-pass exchanger with area in the tens of m² is in the right ballpark.

assumptions
Steady state; sensible cooling only; constant heat capacities; negligible heat loss. Water cp ≈ 4.18 kJ/kg·K. Allow roughly 10–20% uncertainty for this napkin estimate; area uncertainty can be larger if U is poorly known.

flags
The terminal differences are 55 K and 20 K, giving countercurrent LMTD = (55 − 20)/ln(55/20) ≈ 34.6 K. A 1–2 exchanger requires a correction factor F: A = Q/(U × F × LMTD). Thus, 20 K is a conservative effective assumption, not the calculated countercurrent LMTD. Confirm correction factor, fouling allowance, and pressure drops during sizing.
